chapter_theme: The three words of the great saying tat tvam asi, 'that thou art': 'thou' is the soul known apart from the tattvas, 'that' is Siva, and 'art', the word that joins them, is Shakti. When they mingle the soul becomes Siva in a joy beyond words, and the joining word is matched to the turiya state.
structure_note: The chapter defines the three words (2437 to 2441), gives a breath-yoga way into them (2442), and maps them onto the states of waking, dream and turiya (2443, 2444).

2437.reading: One who reaches 'thou' as it appears, 'that' surrounding it, and 'art' that receives them, becomes the transcendent-immanent so that birth ends, and as the self that took this on dies away, stays as Siva.
2437.nuance: தொம்பதம், தற்பதம், அசிபதம் are the Sanskrit tvam, tat and asi. பராபரம் is the Lord as beyond and within. ஏன்றனன் மாள, 'he who accepted dying', is hard to construe; it may mean the individual self ends in Siva.

2438.reading: Contemplating awareness, and letting go, in the way of nada's end, the distinctions of the elements and the ninety-six instruments that are spoken of, to become the 'thou' that the Veda speaks of is the truth.
2438.nuance: தொண்ணூறுடன் ஓராறு (ninety with six) is the count of 96 tattvas common in Tamil Siddha writing, beside the 36 used elsewhere in the Tirumanthiram. 'Thou' is the soul known in itself once the instruments are set aside.

2439.reading: Whether called 'that' or 'thou', what stands in 'art' is the station of the finely jewelled lady, and Siva, whom no word can follow, stood mingled there without any fancy.
2439.nuance: The verse makes the joining word, asi, Shakti (நேரிழையாள், the woman of fine jewels): the bond between soul and Lord is his power. கற்பனை யின்றி (without imagining) says the mingling is real, not a construct of thought.

2440.reading: When the soul and the Supreme, joined in 'art', mingle with Siva who has no seam, it appears, once words cease, as a joy without equal, like milk, honey and nectar.
2440.nuance: அணு is the soul. கணு ஒன்று இலாத, without a single node (as on a cane), is an image of seamless wholeness. உரையற்றிட, when speech ends, is the condition for the joy to appear.

2441.reading: With 'thou', 'that' and 'art' appearing, the trusting soul stands as the Supreme and as Siva; that word is the saying whose form is the highest, and glorious Nandi rules and gives its true meaning.
2441.nuance: சீவன் பரன் சிவன் may be read as matching the three words to soul, Supreme and Siva. வாக்கியம் (the saying) is the Upanishadic great saying; Tirumular makes Nandi, his guru, the one who gives its sense.

2442.reading: Even some who do not know the fifty letters, seeking the Highest within the three-word teaching and driving the breath that is the true Supreme, become, by that supreme yoga, He himself.
2442.nuance: ஐம்பது (the fifty) is taken as the fifty letters of the mantra alphabet, or learning in general; வாசி is the breath in Siddha yoga. உம்பனை is obscure, perhaps 'the one on high'. The verse opens the way to those without learning.

2443.reading: When knowledge, extinguished, slips away it is the state beyond; when the senses and sound and the rest are let go it becomes vast; and the beginningless one sets going the states of waking and the rest, the three, two, one and five.
2443.nuance: நந்தி may be the Lord's name or the verb 'extinguished' (நந்துதல்), and நந்திய in line 3 likewise; the reading changes with it. The numbers மூன்றுஇரண்டு ஒன்று ஐந்து are traditionally the instruments active in each state, but the verse does not say which.

2444.reading: In the supreme turiya, waking is absorbed; in its spreading is dream; in its stilling is turiya, with the sushumna, and cessation at Siva; and that rare turiya is 'art'.
2444.nuance: கழுமுனை is the sushumna, the central channel. The verse maps the joining word asi onto the turiya state, so the three words and the states of consciousness become one scheme. Its step-by-step order is compressed.

links.note: 2425 makes the Lord's foot Shakti as grace, which brings the soul to knowledge; 2439 makes 'art', the word that joins soul and Lord, the station of Shakti.
2443 has the Lord setting going waking and the other states; 2444 places them inside the supreme turiya and names its rare turiya as the joining word.

2146 counts the instruments of the first state as ninety-six (ஆதி அவத்தைக் கருவி தொண்ணூற்றாறே): elements, senses, malas, gunas and adharas. 2438 says that letting go of those same instruments (கருவி தொண்ணூறுடன் ஓராறு) at nada's end is how one becomes the 'thou' the Veda speaks of. 2438 takes 2146's inventory and makes discarding it the way to know the soul.

2438 says the soul becomes 'thou' by letting go of the ninety-six instruments. Thiruppugazh 314 calls Murugan the common ground that holds all the ninety-six tattvas yet stands free of them (சகலமும் பற்றிப் பற்றற நிற்கும்). The same count of ninety-six appears for what the soul must drop and for what the Lord holds without clinging.

965 says the fifty letters are all the Vedas and Agamas, and once one knows what they become, they become the five letters. 2442 says even some who do not know the fifty (ஐம்பது அறியாதவரும்) become He by the three-word teaching and the breath. 2442 opens a way to the goal that does not depend on the mastery of letters 965 describes.

source_issues: 2442: உம்பனை and தம்பரயோகம் (perhaps தற்பரயோகம்) are obscure and may be corrupt.
